title: Strix Models — Training Data Schema
description: What each model in apps/models/*.pth was trained on. Sourced from apps/notebooks/*, apps/models/MANIFEST.json, apps/models/registry.json, gnn_metadata.pkl, selected_features_top25.json, feature_names.pkl, feature_matrix_no_leakage.parquet, labels.parquet. The runtime FeatureMessage (see docs/log_stream_schema.json) reproduces the same 55-d vector from live Wazuh alerts.

see_also.raw_column_inventory: docs/DATASET_SCHEMA.md — exhaustive 176-column raw-field inventory with null %, unique counts, examples, and which columns are leaky.
see_also.runtime_stream_reference: docs/log_stream_schema.json — per-stage runtime envelopes (RawAlertMessage → FeatureMessage → VerdictMessage → WS frames).
see_also.model_registry: apps/models/registry.json — weight checksums, architecture summaries, model versions.
see_also.preprocessing_artifacts: apps/models/MANIFEST.json — sha256 + provenance for each pickle (scaler, PCAs, calibrator, GNN metadata).

source_dataset.name: Linux-APT-Dataset-2024
source_dataset.alternate_path_in_notebooks: Linux-APT-Dataset-2024/combine.csv (cited in preprocessing_dataset.ipynb — earlier filename for the same data)
source_dataset.format: Wazuh alerts exported from an Elasticsearch / OpenSearch `wazuh-alerts-4.x-*` index — flattened `_source.*` records, one alert per row.
source_dataset.raw_column_groups_in_xlsx: envelope (4) · core (8) · agent (3) · manager (1) · predecoder (3) · decoder (4) · rule (19) · rule-mitre (6) · data-audit (36) · data-sca (39) · data-other (25) · syscheck (22) · labels (6) — see docs/DATASET_SCHEMA.md §4 for the full inventory.
source_dataset.filter_applied: Keep only rows where rule.mitre_tactics OR rule.mitre_techniques is non-null and matches the MITRE pattern (TAxxxx / Txxxx[.yyy]).
source_dataset.leakage_dropped_reason: These fields encode the label or a near-perfect proxy of the label (Wazuh's own decision). Including them in features would let the model trivially memorise — see GNN Part 2 retrain ('NO RULE LEVEL'), which removed rule_level and re-fit on the remaining 55 columns. The live-inference normalizer (apps/api/.../wazuh_adapter.py) strips the same fields before publishing.
live_inference_caveats: Labels (`malicious`, `cyber_kill_chain_*`) are synthesized at preprocessing time and DO NOT exist in raw Wazuh alerts. Live inference outputs them, never reads them.

Timestamp format in the xlsx export is Kibana-Discover CSV style: `Mon DD, YYYY @ HH:MM:SS.mmm`. Live Wazuh alerts ship ISO-8601 `@timestamp`. The normalization service must parse both — pd.to_datetime(..., errors='coerce') handles both.

Many raw columns are mutually-exclusive alert-type views: an auditd alert fills `_source.data.audit.*` and leaves `_source.syscheck.*` empty (and vice versa). The engineered pipeline ends with fillna(0) to absorb this.
`cyber_kill_chain_id` is 100% null in the export — drop.
`_source.data.status` has a single observed value ('DENIED') and is 100% null — never one-hot.
Training was single-site (5 agents / one /24). `ip_is_private` generalises; agent-specific one-hots would not — the committed engineering code deliberately avoids them.

secbert_cmd_16: cmd_secbert_emb_0..15 — PCA(16) of SecBERT[768] over the parsed command string
secbert_log_16: log_secbert_emb_0..15 — PCA(16) of SecBERT[768] over the raw full_log line

selected_55d.rationale: feature_selection_final.ipynb scored the 119 engineered features and kept the top-25 *conceptual* features. SecBERT contributes 2 conceptual slots (log + cmd) but expands to 32 actual columns (16 each), giving 23 individual + 32 SecBERT = 55 final columns.

ae_vae_numeric_ordering.definition: selected_features_top25.json `all_selected_columns` — SecBERT block in NUMERIC string order: emb_0, emb_1, emb_2, ..., emb_15.

gnn_alphabetical_ordering.definition: gnn_metadata.pkl['features'] — SecBERT block in PYTHON STRING (alphabetical) order: emb_0, emb_1, emb_10, emb_11, ..., emb_15, emb_2, emb_3, ..., emb_9.
gnn_alphabetical_ordering.runtime_handling: PreprocessingPipeline.transform_for_gnn(vec) re-permutes the AE/VAE-ordered vector into the GNN order at inference time.

scaler.fitted_on: training-set 55-d feature matrix (the columns above) — applied at inference before any model forward pass.

labels.synthesis_rule: `malicious` and `cyber_kill_chain_*` columns are NOT native Wazuh fields. They were derived at preprocessing time: `malicious=1` when the alert has non-null `_source.rule.mitre_techniques` OR `_source.rule.mitre_tactics` (preprocessing_dataset.ipynb cell ~52). `cyber_kill_chain_tactic` is a mapping of MITRE tactic → 5-stage CKC bucket (cell ~58–62).

columns.name: malicious
columns.description: Binary attack label. Used by AE (anomaly target indirectly), VAE calibrator (LogReg target), and GNN (node-level supervised target).

columns.name: cyber_kill_chain_tactic
columns.description: Symbolic kill-chain bucket — 5-stage taxonomy used by the notebook. ~78.8% null (Unknown) because only MITRE-tagged rows get a stage.
columns.doc_data_discrepancy: docs/DATASET_SCHEMA.md §1 lists S4=16,556 (Install/Exploit) and S3=4,291 (Delivery) — those two are SWAPPED relative to the actual labels.parquet. Treat the parquet (`S3`=16,556 / `S4`=4,291) as authoritative for what the models trained on; the .md table is stale on this row.

columns.name: ckc_encoded
columns.description: Numeric CKC stage. 8-class output target of the Transformer (numCkcStages=8 in registry.json), even though only 6 classes appear in training data. NOTE: this notebook-internal encoding uses 5 = Unknown (benign), which is DIFFERENT from the *runtime* CKC mapping where 0 = BENIGN. Don't conflate the two encodings.

columns.name: cyber_kill_chain_id
columns.description: 100% null in the export. Drop at load time.

labels.leakage_note: rule.level was excluded from features after Part-1 GNN training because it acted as a near-perfect proxy for `malicious` (Wazuh's own severity score). Part-2 GNN retrains on the 55-d vector with rule_level dropped — that is the model shipped in apps/models/gnn_model.pth.

ae.loss: MSE reconstruction loss; anomaly_score derived from per-sample recon_error (higher = more anomalous).
ae.training_target: no explicit class label — unsupervised reconstruction. The `malicious` column is used at evaluation time only.

output.uncertainty: predictive variance over the latent posterior

calibrator.output: P(malicious) ∈ [0,1] — what becomes vaeMaliciousProb at inference
calibrator.trained_on: VAE recon_loss vs `malicious` label; coef_.shape=(1,1), intercept_=-5.4128

input.description: Sequence of AE-latent vectors per host session — the AE's 64-d bottleneck, oldest→newest with the current event appended.

transformer.loss: CrossEntropy on `ckc_encoded` (next event in the sequence).

input_edges.construction_rule: Connect alerts that share the same agent_id within `intra_window_sec` (intra-host edges), and alerts on different hosts that share `srcip` or `srcuser` within `cross_window_sec` (cross-host edges).

gnn.rule_level_note: Part-1 of the notebook included rule_level as feature #56 and overfit (precision/recall ~1.0 because rule_level encodes the label). Part-2 slices `X_scaled[:, :-1]` to drop rule_level and retrains — the shipped model is the Part-2 weights.

dqn.trained_in: RL_agent/ (separate training repo, hyperparameters mirrored in registry.json)

input.description: Assembled at inference by `core.state_builder.build_state` from the outputs of the four prior models + the chain session state. Never appears in any single training file — the DQN was trained in a simulator that produces the same 13-d state.

runtime_to_training_correspondence.summary: Each FeatureMessage emitted at runtime carries a 55-float feature_vector reproducing the training-time AE/VAE column order. The inference worker re-permutes into the GNN ordering on the fly. The Transformer reads the AE's 64-d latent (no separate features). The DQN reads a 13-d state assembled from the previous models' outputs.
runtime_to_training_correspondence.diagram: Wazuh alert → adapter (drop leakage cols) → preprocessor (one-hot decoder/location, SecBERT→PCA) → 55-d vector (numeric order) → AE+VAE  ;  re-permute → 55-d vector (alphabetical order) → GNN  ;  AE.latent[64] → Transformer  ;  {AE,VAE,Transformer,GNN outputs + session state} → 13-d state → DQN → action
